meta.title: Adrian P. Janczenia - Backend Developer
meta.description: Portfolio of Adrian P. Janczenia. Backend, microservices and an interactive look at the site architecture.

hero.title: I design, develop and maintain backend systems.
hero.body: I am a software engineer with several years of backend development experience and a solid background in testing. I specialize in distributed systems and microservices built with Go and PHP. I focus on the quality of the solutions I build, as well as code clarity and maintainability. I follow sound engineering practices and value effective, clear communication within a team.

career_snapshot.title: From testing to backend development
career_snapshot.body: I worked in testing and test automation from 2018, and have developed backend systems since 2022. This experience helps me think about contracts, data and the reliability of the entire flow.

site_teaser.title: See how it works behind the scenes
site_teaser.body: This portfolio runs on Go services. An interactive map shows how requests travel through its microservices and highlights the technologies behind them.

intro.title: The work that shaped my approach
intro.body: From testing and test automation to developing backend services. The career path below describes my work and responsibilities.

backend.title: Backend Developer
backend.summary: Development and maintenance of an e-commerce platform
tasks: Building scalable microservices in Go and maintaining legacy PHP systems
Contributing to the migration of a monolithic system to Go microservices
Building distributed systems with RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, Redis and REST APIs
Rewriting and optimizing older microservices to improve performance and maintainability
Maintaining code quality through unit and functional tests and regular code reviews
Automating CI/CD pipelines with TeamCity and GitHub Actions and managing infrastructure with Docker and Ansible
Working in an Agile (Kanban) environment with an emphasis on clean code and sound engineering practices

qa.title: QA Engineer
qa.summary: QA engineer focused on test automation, business logic and data flow validation
tasks: Developing automated tests with Python (Behave, Selenium) and PHP (Codeception)
Validating data integrity and business logic in RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, MSSQL and Redis
Performing comprehensive API tests and debugging systems with Postman
Analyzing requirements and maintaining test documentation in an Agile/Scrum environment
Manually testing complex web applications and reporting defects

migration.title: From monolith to microservices
migration.summary: Contributed to migrating a large e-commerce platform to Go services
migration.problem: A monolith developed over many years needed to be gradually split into smaller, more manageable microservices.
contribution: Built and developed microservices in Go
Kept the new services working with the existing PHP code
Worked with PostgreSQL, Redis, REST APIs and RabbitMQ, as well as tests and code reviews
migration.result: Individual functions were gradually extracted into microservices that can be developed and maintained independently.
migration.takeaway: Reliability, compatible contracts and safe deployment of changes were the priorities.

checkout.title: Checkout and payments
checkout.summary: Worked on the backend order flow, integrations and payments
checkout.problem: A complex checkout process connected multiple services, asynchronous communication and external APIs.
contribution: Developed backend services across the order flow
Contributed to the design of interfaces and integrations with external APIs
Worked with multiple microservices using RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL and Redis, and wrote tests and reviewed code
checkout.result: The order flow evolved through collaboration between services, with error handling taken into account.
checkout.takeaway: Checkout depends on the entire flow, from service contracts to the response shown to the customer. That flow must be reliable.

reservation.title: Product reservation list
reservation.summary: Implemented a product reservation list for an e-commerce platform
reservation.problem: Limited product availability called for clear rules to secure an item for a customer.
contribution: Integrated the feature into the existing backend
Used tests and code reviews to support the reliability of the implementation
reservation.result: The new feature became part of the existing microservices.
reservation.takeaway: A small interface change can have a significant impact on the existing logic in backend services.

common.request_reaches_frontend: The request reaches the front end.

content.rendering_overview: To display a page, the front end retrieves content from the content service through the API gateway. The service uses data loaded into memory at startup.
content.unknown_language_uses_polish: When the URL contains an unknown language, the front end selects the Polish version.
content.the_front_end_starts_ssr: The front end starts building the HTML page on the server (SSR).
content.gateway_forwards_the_request: The API gateway forwards the request to the content service.
content.request_content_from_gateway: The front end asks the API gateway for content in the selected language.
content.render_service_error_page: The front end displays an error page using the shared template.
content.gateway_failure_stops_rendering: A connection failure or timeout at the API gateway prevents the page from being rendered.
content.json_loaded_on_startup_no_file_read: JSON files are loaded when the service starts; they are not read again for every request.
content.polish_fallback_forwarded: The front end has requested Polish content instead of an unknown language.
content.content_service_chooses_a_language: The content service selects the appropriate language.
content.localized_content_response: The service returns content prepared for the selected language.
content.render_html_from_content: The front end combines the content with a template to produce HTML.
content.rendered_html_response_path: The completed HTML travels from the front end through the reverse proxy to the browser.

pow.challenge_request_overview: This is a separate request. The server returns task data (a seed), and the browser searches for a trial number (nonce) on your device before requesting a CAPTCHA image.
pow.captcha_service_signs_seed: The CAPTCHA service prepares task data and protects it with a signature.
pow.browser_requests_challenge: The browser requests a computational task that helps block bots.
pow.hmac_secret_remains_private: The signature lets the service verify where the task came from without revealing the secret HMAC key.
pow.seed_response_precedes_nonce_search: The task data returns to the browser. Only then does it start searching for a nonce.

captcha.pow_and_captcha_image: From the anti-bot task to a CAPTCHA image
captcha.prior_challenge_context: The browser has already fetched task data with GET /api/pow. Here you can choose the valid solution or one reason for rejecting the same POST request.
captcha.nonce_calculated_in_browser: The browser performs the calculations locally without sending more requests to the server.
captcha.nonce_search_visualization: The browser tries successive nonce values until the SHA-256 result meets the required difficulty.
captcha.validate_pow_signature_time_hash: Check the signature, expiry and SHA-256 result
captcha.captcha_service_receives_request: The request reaches the CAPTCHA service.
captcha.signature_mismatch_no_redis_write: The signature is invalid. Nothing is written to Redis.
captcha.challenge_expired_no_redis_write: The task has expired. Nothing is written to Redis.
captcha.weak_hash_no_redis_write: The computational result is too weak. Nothing is written to Redis.
captcha.reject_captcha_creation: Refuse to create a CAPTCHA image
captcha.invalid_solution_not_stored: Validation stops the request before the task is marked as used.
captcha.key_already_exists: Redis already has a record that this task was used.
captcha.atomic_seed_reuse_check: Redis writes the record only if the key does not yet exist. This operation is atomic (SETNX).
captcha.redis_rejects_reuse: Redis detects that the task has already been used.
captcha.the_seed_can_be_used_once: The same task data can be used only once.
captcha.a_reused_seed_creates_no_new_image: Reusing the task does not create another CAPTCHA image.
captcha.captcha_receives_a_short_ttl: The CAPTCHA session receives a short expiry time.
captcha.the_rejection_returns_to_the_client: The rejection returns to the browser.
captcha.the_image_returns_to_the_browser: The CAPTCHA image returns to the browser.

verify.verification_overview: The service compares the answer with the session state in Redis. A correct answer marks the session as solved; the visitor can then request access to the CV.
verify.captcha_session_lookup: The CAPTCHA service looks for the session associated with the image.
verify.captcha_answer_arrives: The answer reaches the CAPTCHA service.
verify.solved_session_ready_for_cv: The solved session can be used to request CV access.
verify.atomic_captcha_state_update: A Redis script changes the session state in one atomic operation.
verify.the_client_may_request_a_cv_token: The browser can now request a CV download token.
verify.verification_error_returned: The browser receives information about the incorrect answer.
verify.verification_result_to_form: The result returns to the CV download form.

cvtoken.cv_token_request_overview: The API gateway routes the public /api/cv-token request to the internal /api/v1/cv-request path. The request then reaches the content service through RabbitMQ.
cvtoken.gateway_sends_token_rpc: The API gateway forwards /api/v1/cv-request through RabbitMQ.
cvtoken.cv_form_submits_access_code: The form sends the access code and the ID of the solved CAPTCHA.
cvtoken.token_request_reaches_content: The request reaches the content service.
cvtoken.token_request_delivered_by_rpc: RabbitMQ delivers the request and enables the reply (RPC).
cvtoken.validate_and_store_state: Validate the data and store the token
cvtoken.captcha_and_code_are_valid: The access code is correct and the CAPTCHA has been solved.
cvtoken.validation_denies_the_token: The data does not meet the requirements for issuing a token.
cvtoken.a_short_lived_token_is_ready: The single-use token is ready and will expire soon.
cvtoken.invalid_input_does_not_issue_a_token: Invalid data does not create a new token.
cvtoken.token_response_to_dialog: The token returns to the CV download dialog.
cvtoken.dialog_displays_generic_error: The dialog shows an error without disclosing verification details.
cvtoken.token_rpc_response_path: The reply returns through RabbitMQ and the API gateway to the browser.

download.download_order_overview: The content service opens the correct PDF first, then consumes the single-use token in Redis. After a successful download, repeating the same request returns 410.
download.download_and_retry: Download the CV and try again
download.token_language_mismatch: Language does not match the token
download.gateway_calls_download_service: The API gateway calls the content service over HTTP.
download.download_request_arrives: The request reaches the CV download service.
download.file_failure_precedes_token_use: The file-open error occurs before any attempt to consume the token.
download.the_file_is_ready_to_stream: The file is ready to be sent to the browser.
download.missing_pdf_preserves_token: A missing file does not consume the token.
download.the_error_returns_to_the_browser: The error returns to the browser.
download.key_missing: The token does not exist in Redis
download.language_matches_token_is_consumed: The language matches, so the token is consumed.
download.language_mismatch_token_remains: The language does not match, so the token remains valid.
download.atomic_token_validation: A Redis script checks the token and makes the decision in one atomic operation.
download.the_pdf_returns_as_a_stream: The PDF file is sent to the browser.
download.download_response_path: The response passes through the gateway and front end.
download.retry_reaches_content_service: The same request reaches the content service again.
download.retry_reuses_token: The second attempt uses the same token.
download.pdf_available_token_may_be_gone: The file is still available, but the single-use token may already have been consumed.
download.retry_checks_pdf_before_token: On the second attempt, the service again checks the file before the token.
download.the_token_was_already_consumed: The token was consumed during the first download.
download.consumed_token_missing_in_redis: Redis can no longer find the single-use token.
download.a_repeat_download_is_not_possible: The same token cannot download the CV twice.
download.the_rejection_returns_to_the_browser: The rejection returns to the browser.

route.unknown_route_overview: The front end handles an unknown URL itself. The request’s Accept header determines whether the browser receives an HTML page or an API client receives JSON. No other service is called.
route.frontend_detects_unknown_route: The front end recognizes that this URL does not exist.
route.the_request_stops_at_the_front_end: The front end handles the request without calling other services.
route.shared_error_template: The browser receives a page built from the shared error template.
route.json_response_for_api: The API client receives error details in JSON.
route.frontend_returns_404_locally: The front end returns HTTP 404 without contacting the API gateway.

components.browser_responsibilities: Displays the page, runs JavaScript, performs the anti-bot calculations and sends requests from the CV form.
components.caddy_responsibilities: Receives site traffic, forwards it to the front end, adds security headers and redirects the address without “www”. It may be omitted in a local environment.
components.frontend_responsibilities: This Go service builds pages on the server, selects the Polish or English version, and handles site URLs, errors and the CV download dialog.
components.gateway_responsibilities: The API gateway receives requests from the front end and routes them to the appropriate services over gRPC, RabbitMQ or HTTP.
components.rabbitmq_responsibilities: Carries the CV token request from the API gateway to the content service and delivers the reply.
components.content_service_responsibilities: Provides Polish and English site content, issues single-use CV tokens and sends the appropriate PDF file.
components.content_cache_responsibilities: Polish and English content from JSON files is loaded into memory when the service starts. It is not a separate service, and files are not read again for each request.
components.captcha_service_responsibilities: Prepares the anti-bot task, checks its solution, creates a CAPTCHA image and verifies the entered answer.
components.redis_responsibilities: Stores short-lived state for anti-bot tasks, CAPTCHA sessions and CV tokens. Atomic operations prevent single-use data from being reused.

branches.render_polish_page: Display the Polish version of the page.
branches.render_english_page: Display the English version of the page.
branches.fallback_for_unknown_language: An unknown language in the URL selects the Polish version.
branches.unavailable_gateway_error: An unavailable API gateway causes the 503 error page to appear.
branches.fetch_pow_challenge: The browser fetches signed anti-bot task data.
branches.valid_nonce_creates_captcha: A valid computational result allows a CAPTCHA image to be created.
branches.invalid_signature_rejected: An invalid signature causes the task to be rejected.
branches.expired_seed_rejected: The task is rejected after it expires.
branches.weak_pow_rejected: The SHA-256 result does not meet the required difficulty.
branches.seed_reuse_rejected: Reusing the same task data is rejected.
branches.correct_answer_solves_captcha: A correct answer marks the CAPTCHA session as solved.
branches.wrong_answer_reduces_attempts: An incorrect answer reduces the number of remaining attempts.
branches.expired_captcha_rejected: A CAPTCHA answer is rejected after the session expires.
branches.valid_cv_access_issues_token: A valid access code and solved CAPTCHA allow a short-lived token to be issued.
branches.wrong_access_code_rejected: An incorrect access code does not allow a token to be issued.
branches.unsolved_captcha_rejected: An unsolved CAPTCHA prevents a token from being issued.
branches.expired_captcha_token_rejected: An expired CAPTCHA session prevents a token from being issued.
branches.first_download_then_retry: The first request returns a PDF file. Repeating it with the same token returns 410.
branches.language_mismatch_keeps_token: Choosing a language that does not match the token does not consume it.
branches.expired_token_rejected: The download is rejected after the token expires.
branches.missing_pdf_keeps_token: A missing PDF file causes an error, but the token remains available.
branches.browser_html_404: The browser receives an HTML page with status 404.
branches.api_json_404: The API client receives a JSON response with status 404.

items.text: The controller of personal data processed in connection with the use of www.adrianjanczenia.dev is Adrian Janczenia. For privacy-related matters, you can write to contact@adrianjanczenia.dev.

When you visit the website, technical data needed to handle your request are processed, in particular your IP address, the date and time, the requested page address, the server response code, and information sent by your browser. Some of these data are recorded in access logs. I use them to provide the website, detect abuse, and diagnose errors.

Downloading my CV requires an access code and solving a CAPTCHA. The service processes these data, as well as short-lived identifiers and download tokens, solely to verify access to the file and protect this feature against abuse.

The website has no contact form, user accounts, or newsletter. You can copy the email address shown on the website or use the link to your email application. Only when you send a message do I receive your email address, the message content, and any attachments. I use them to correspond with you and respond.

The legal basis for processing access-log data, handling CV downloads, and correspondence is my legitimate interest in operating and securing the website and responding to messages — Article 6(1)(f) of the GDPR. Sending a message is voluntary; without a return email address, I cannot reply.
I keep website access logs for no longer than 7 days. CAPTCHA state and CV download tokens have short validity periods and expire automatically.
I delete email correspondence within 30 days after the conversation ends, meaning the last message on a given matter. I do not create my own backups of access logs or correspondence.

The website runs on infrastructure that I administer, using a VPS. The VPS provider is involved in operating the website, and an email service provider is involved in handling correspondence. They may process data to the extent necessary to provide their services. I do not share visitor data with advertisers.
The website does not use cookies for analytics, advertising, or profiling. Browsing the public website does not require an account or login.

The website contains links to external services, including GitHub and LinkedIn. Merely viewing my portfolio does not open those services. After you click a link, the operator of the destination website determines how your data are processed.

To the extent provided by the GDPR, you may request access to your data, their rectification or erasure, and restriction of processing. You may also object to processing based on my legitimate interest. To do so, write to contact@adrianjanczenia.dev. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the President of the Personal Data Protection Office in Poland.
